# Prioritize

Turns Triage into an ordered Todo queue. The order comes from what each issue needs and what the code looks like today, and it is recorded in the issue **Relationships** (blocked by / blocking), which you read **and write**. Reuses `/triage` for labels and agent briefs. Rubrics and the comment template: [RUBRICS.md](RUBRICS.md).

Every comment must start with: `> *This was generated by AI during triage.*`

```bash
Q=~/.claude/skills/prioritize/scripts/queue.sh
B=~/.claude/skills/project-board/scripts/board.sh
R=~/.claude/skills/project-board/scripts/blockers.sh
```

## 1. Read the queue

`$Q` returns JSON: the issues in Triage and Todo in board order (number, title, `column`, labels, `hasAcceptance`, `blockedBy` with each blocker's `state` and board `status`, `blocking`). With no board (`board: null`) it returns all open issues; skip those that already have a `Queue position:` comment. The repo must have one linked board or none.

## 2. Understand each issue and the code

Read the issue and its comments (`gh issue view <n> --comments`), `CONTEXT.md` and `docs/adr/` if present, then explore the code with Grep, Glob and Read, and `git log` for recent work. Go through the checklist in RUBRICS.md. Write down per issue: what exists already, what it touches, what it needs from other issues.

## 3. Fix the relationships

The Relationships are the model of the order, so make them right before ranking:

- Add a missing blocker: `$R add <n> <blocker>` when `<n>` needs something the blocker creates, or both change the same code.
- Remove a wrong one: `$R remove <n> <blocker>` only when clearly unnecessary. Leave relationships that someone set on purpose when in doubt.
- Explain every change in the issue comment. `$R list <n>` shows the result; `add` refuses a direct cycle, check longer cycles yourself.

## 4. Check readiness, set Priority, Size, Estimate

**Ready** = a clear description, acceptance criteria and no `needs-info`, `wontfix` or `dup` label. Not ready: stays in Triage, add the `needs-info` label (`gh label create needs-info --force` first if missing), comment what is missing, point to `/triage`. Size XL: stays in Triage, recommend splitting with `/to-issues`.

Choose Priority, Size and Estimate with RUBRICS.md. Issues already in Todo keep their values unless empty.

## 5. Order

1. A blocker is **settled** when it is closed, or its column is Done, Todo, Doing, Review or Testing, or it is ranked earlier in this run. In-progress blockers count because the coder only starts an issue whose blockers are done. An open blocker that is not on the board is not settled: the dependent stays in Triage and the comment names it.
2. Queue an issue only when all its blockers are settled. A blocker that is not ready (or XL) keeps its dependents in Triage. A cycle: queue none of it, continue with the rest, report it.
3. Among the issues that may be queued (including those already in Todo), pick by: higher Priority, then the one that blocks more issues, then smaller Size, then lower number. Repeat until none is left.

## 6. Queue in order

For each ranked issue that comes from Triage, one at a time:

```bash
$B claim <n> Triager
$B set <n> Priority P1 && $B set <n> Size M && $B set <n> Estimate 6 && $B move <n> todo
```

`move` also clears the Agent field; if a step fails, run `$B release <n>` before reporting. Then fix the column order explicitly with all queued issues, Triage ones and existing Todo ones, in rank order: `$B order <n1> <n2> <n3> ...` (first = top, the coder takes the top). Check with `$Q` that Todo shows that order. Post the comments (RUBRICS.md).

## No board

The same commands run and print `SKIPPED` for the board parts (`order` too). Study, fix relationships and rank, set and move nothing, and post the proposed order in the comments. The handover is manual.

## Report

End with a table: order, issue, Priority, Size, relationships changed, and the reason for every issue left in Triage.
